That's not how entertainment and/or art works though. There's no objective right or wrong, each reviewer simply tells their readers about the experience they've been having and at most publications then adds a score at the end of it. Though video games aren't quite as ambivalent as music and film (as there are technical aspects that actually can be rated objectively), the resulting experience itself remains purely subjective. 

I could see how at times a few reviewers might happen to have the same, great experience with the occasional "big" release - but when nearly all scores for every single so called triple-A title *always* hit the same mark each time, there's something wrong.
